Please contact the airline for additional information.  
Investigation and Other Information

## Key Details of Recent Plane Crash Reports (2013–2026)
Emergency responders rushed to the scene but were unable to save the pilot. The Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board have been notified and will investigate the circumstances surrounding the Oregon crash.
**Midair Collision of Vintage Aircraft Near Lancaster Kills Veteran Pilot Ryder Adams**| September 22, 2024
Amidair collisionbetween two vintage aircraft over Lancaster, California, on Sunday afternoon resulted in the death of Ryder Adams, 62. A respected member of the precision-flying Tiger Squadron, Adams was piloting a 1985 Nanchang CJ-6A when it collided with a Soviet-era Yakovlev Yak-52 around 12:50 p.m., according to local reports. The pilot of the Yak-52 survived with minor injuries after managing to crash-land nearby. The incident occurred in the skies above the Los Angeles suburb, with debris scattered near 47th Street East and 60th Street East. The National Transportation Safety Board has launched an investigation.
**Small Plane Crash in Hawthorne, CA Leaves Two Critically Injured**| September 6, 2024
A single-engine Piper Comanche aircraft crash-landed on El Segundo Boulevard in Hawthorne, California, early Friday morning, critically injuring its two occupants. The plane, which caught fire upon impact, was believed to be preparing to land at nearby Hawthorne Airport when it crashed at approximately 12:40 a.m. Emergency responders quickly extinguished the flames and transported the pilot and passenger to a local hospital. Both were listed in critical condition.
A witness who was charging his Tesla nearby rushed to assist in extracting a man from the wreckage before a potential explosion. Remarkably, no injuries were reported on the ground, and surrounding buildings escaped damage. The Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board have launched investigations to determine the cause of the crash.
**Wyoming Plane Crash Kills One, Injures Another in Ash-Scattering Flight**| September 1, 2024
A single-engine plane crash near Francs Peak in Wyoming's Absaroka Mountain Range resulted in one fatality and one serious injury on Sunday. Mary Lou Sanderson, 78, of Lake Havasu, Arizona, was killed in the incident, while the unidentified male pilot survived and was transported to a hospital in Billings with serious injuries.

## Key Details of Recent Plane Crash Reports (2013–2026)
The crash occurred around 11:00 a.m. during a flight intended to scatter Sanderson's husband's ashes. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating the crash of the American Champion 8GCBC aircraft, which also sparked a small fire in the remote area of Shoshone National Forest. A preliminary report on the Wyoming plane crash is expected in the next few weeks.
**Cessna Plane Crash in Oregon Suburb Kills Three**| August 31, 2024
A twin-engine Cessna 421C crashed into a Fairview, Oregon, townhouse on Saturday morning, killing three people. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) reported that the aircraft was attempting to land at Troutdale Airport when it encountered control issues, as indicated by air traffic control recordings. During its descent, the plane struck a power pole before crashing into a townhouse complex, igniting a fire. According to reports, two people on the plane were killed, along with a woman in the townhouse. NTSB officials stated that the incident occurred during a routine maintenance flight and that a full investigation could take up to 18 months.
**Engine Failure Cited as Potential Cause of Cessna Crash That Killed Pilot**| July 16, 2024
A pilot was killed when a twin-engine Cessna plane crashed into the Tred Avon River,in Talbot County, Maryland on Tuesday morning. Maryland State Police reported that the crash occurred at around 9:35 a.m. local time near Travelers Rest Circle in Easton. The pilot, who was the only person onboard, was found deceased in the water. The FAA said the pilot reported engine failure shortly before the fatal crash. Authorities say the University Research Foundation owned the plane.
**Crop Dusting Planes Collide in Idaho**| June 20, 2024
Two crop-dusting airplanes collided midair just west of the Arco airport in Idaho. One of the pilots was killed, and another sustained life-threatening injuries. The pilots have not been publicly identified.
The Butte County Sheriff’s Office received an emergency call at approximately 12:30 p.m. local time noting that the planes had crashed near the intersection of 3600 West and US 26/93.

## Key Details of Recent Plane Crash Reports (2013–2026)
The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) will investigate the crash. A preliminary report is expected in a few weeks.
**Man Killed in Auburn Plane Crash**| June 6, 2024
An unidentified man was killed on Thursday afternoon when the small plane he was piloting crashed into a building in Auburn, Washington. The fatal plane crash happened at around 12:15 p.m. local time near the 400 block of C Street Northwest. No one inside the building was harmed in the crash. Authorities are investigating the cause of the crash. A preliminary report is expected in the coming weeks.
**Plane Crash Kills Baton Rouge Plastic Surgeon Lucuis “Tre” Doucet and Two Children**| May 15, 2024
Three people were killed in a small plane crash in Williamson County on Wednesday afternoon. At 12:05 p.m., a local resident notified Williamson County 911 about a plane breaking apart mid-air and crashing. Authorities say the single-engine Beechcraft V35, was en route from Baton Rouge, Louisiana, to Louisville, Kentucky, when it went down near Bending Chestnut Road in the Leipers Fork area, less than a mile from Natchez Trace Parkway.
The three deceased victims were identified as Lucius “Tre” Doucet, a plastic surgeon from Baton Rouge, and two of his adult children, Giselle and Jean Luc. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating the fatal crash in Franklin.
The agency’s preliminary report included eyewitness accounts of a loud "pop” as the plane was overhead. Video footage showed pieces of the airplane descending through an overcast cloud layer. The debris was scattered in a fan-like pattern with a radius exceeding half a mile.
Officials recovered about 90% of the plane's wreckage, which included separated elevator rudders and wings, main fuselage fragments, seats, the instrument panel, engine, and propeller assembly. Some parts were found submerged in eight feet of water in a lake. According to the NTSB report, “[t]he deformation of the stabilizer spars on both sides exhibited features consistent with downward failure. A final report is expected to be completed in the next year.

## Key Details of Recent Plane Crash Reports (2013–2026)
**One Dead in Modoc County, California Plane Crash**| April 9, 2024
A 69-year-old man was killed when a single-engine plane crashed between Alturas and Likely near County Road 60 in Modoc County. The plane was an agricultural plane used for crop dusting or spraying pesticides. However, it was not carrying any pesticides at the time of the crash. Authorities have identified the victim as Peter J. Spyres of Arbuckle, California. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating the cause of the crash.
**Two Killed in Truckee, CA Plane Crash Identified as Liron and Naomi Petrushka**| March 30, 2024
Two Israeli tech investors were killed when a small plane crashed while attempting to land at Truckee Tahoe Airport. Liron and Naomi Petrushka were in a Daher TBM 700 plane that departed from Centennial Airport in south Denver at 4:22 p.m. MT with a scheduled arrival time at Truckee Tahoe Airport three hours and 16 minutes later. According to media reports, the single-engine turboprop crashed around 6:40 p.m. while approaching the airport.
Preliminary investigations by the Aviation Safety Network suggest that the plane missed its initial approach to the northeast-to-southwest runway at Truckee Tahoe Airport. The plane attempted a go-around maneuver, but instead went into a left-hand stalling spiral, ultimately hitting a tree near the Truckee River.
The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has launched an investigation, which will focus on the actions of the pilot, the single-engine plane, maintenance records, and more.
**Ontario Family of Five Killed in Nashville Plane Crash**| March 4, 2024
A family of five from King Township, Ontario, Canada died on Monday night when their plane crashed on Interstate 40 while attempting to land at John C. Tune Airport in Nashville, Tennessee. Authorities identified the victims as Victor Dotsenko, 43, his wife, Rimma, 39, and the couple’s three children — David, 12, Adam, 10, and Emma, 7.

The plane, which caught fire upon impact, was believed to be preparing to land at nearby Hawthorne Airport when it crashed at approximately 12:40 a.m. Emergency responders quickly extinguished the flames and transported the pilot and passenger to a local hospital. A witness who was charging his Tesla nearby rushed to assist in extracting a man from the wreckage before a potential explosion. According to media reports, the single-engine turboprop crashed around 6:40 p.m. while approaching the airport.
Preliminary investigations by the Aviation Safety Network suggest that the plane missed its initial approach to the northeast-to-southwest runway at Truckee Tahoe Airport. The plane attempted a go-around maneuver, but instead went into a left-hand stalling spiral, ultimately hitting a tree near the Truckee River.

Title: Louisiana doctor, his two children killed in Williamson County plane crash, reports say
Chunks: 0,1
FRANKLIN, Tenn. (WZTV) — Three people were killed in a small plane crash in rural Middle Tennessee, law enforcement confirms.
Video 3
The Williamson County Sheriff's Office says a small aircraft crashed just after noon Wednesday near Bending Chestnut Road and Davis Hollow Road in Franklin. According to the NTSB, it was a Beech V35 aircraft which crashed after experiencing an in-flight break up.
> "When responders arrived, they immediately started searching and sizing up the scene to see if there was a possibility of survivors. It was quickly evident that this would be a search and recovery operation, not a search and rescue operation," said Chief Deputy Mark Elrod.
A 911 caller reported an explosion and a possible plane crash on Wednesday. Multiple agencies responded to the scene, including the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).
The sheriff's office reports the plane left Baton Rouge, LA and was en route to Louisville, KY. There were three individuals on board at the time of the crash, the pilot and two passengers. Williamson County Sheriff's Office Chief Deputy Elrod says all three on board were pronounced dead. Their families have been notified.
The plane was registered to Lucius Doucet III, according to FAA's website, but officials have not yet released the identities of the victims.
According to an Instagram post from Williamson Cosmetic Center in East Baton Rouge Parish, Louisiana, Dr. Lucius Doucet was a surgeon at their office.
"It is with heavy hearts and profound sorry that we must announce the passing of our esteemed colleague and cherished team member, Dr. Doucet on May 15th," the post reads.
Louisiana State University identified the two passengers killed in the crash. In a post on X, LSU says Giselle and Jean-Luc Doucet were killed in the plane crash along with their father. According to the university, the siblings were both scheduled to graduate on Friday.
"This is heartbreaking for the LSU community, but especially for those who know and love these two students, and those who were expecting to share graduation with them," LSU stated in the post.
During a press conference on Thursday, Aaron McCarter with the NTSB says while approaching Franklin, the airplane descended from about 10,000 feet down to about 7,800 feet while the ground speed of the airplane increased, as well as its rate of descent.

> "Shortly there after, credible witnesses that we've already spoken with described the airplane as being at an approximate level altitude with both wings folding backwards and the airplane going violently out of control," said McCarter.
McCarter adds the plane's radar data was lost at about 4,000 feet. Additionally, McCarter said the plane did not have a black box but officials did get two data cards out of the wreckage. Whether there is data on the cards remains to be seen.
Officials say the crash left a large debris field about half a mile long. If you live in the area and find debris on your property, you're asked to contact the Williamson County Sheriff’s Office at 615-790-5550.
Three dead after small plane crash in Williamson County (WZTV)
Witnesses to the accident or those who have surveillance video or other information that could be relevant to the investigation are asked to contact the NTSB at witness@ntsb.gov.
The wreckage is being reassembled in Springfield. Investigators say they will likely release a preliminary report before the end of the month.

FRANKLIN, Tenn. (WZTV) — Three people were killed in a small plane crash in rural Middle Tennessee, law enforcement confirms.
Video 3
The Williamson County Sheriff's Office says a small aircraft crashed just after noon Wednesday near Bending Chestnut Road and Davis Hollow Road in Franklin. According to the NTSB, it was a Beech V35 aircraft which crashed after experiencing an in-flight break up.
> "When responders arrived, they immediately started searching and sizing up the scene to see if there was a possibility of survivors. It was quickly evident that this would be a search and recovery operation, not a search and rescue operation," said Chief Deputy Mark Elrod.
A 911 caller reported an explosion and a possible plane crash on Wednesday. Multiple agencies responded to the scene, including the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).
The sheriff's office reports the plane left Baton Rouge, LA and was en route to Louisville, KY. There were three individuals on board at the time of the crash, the pilot and two passengers. Williamson County Sheriff's Office Chief Deputy Elrod says all three on board were pronounced dead. Their families have been notified.
The plane was registered to Lucius Doucet III, according to FAA's website, but officials have not yet released the identities of the victims.
According to an Instagram post from Williamson Cosmetic Center in East Baton Rouge Parish, Louisiana, Dr. Lucius Doucet was a surgeon at their office.
"It is with heavy hearts and profound sorry that we must announce the passing of our esteemed colleague and cherished team member, Dr. Doucet on May 15th," the post reads.
Louisiana State University identified the two passengers killed in the crash. In a post on X, LSU says Giselle and Jean-Luc Doucet were killed in the plane crash along with their father. According to the university, the siblings were both scheduled to graduate on Friday.
"This is heartbreaking for the LSU community, but especially for those who know and love these two students, and those who were expecting to share graduation with them," LSU stated in the post.
During a press conference on Thursday, Aaron McCarter with the NTSB says while approaching Franklin, the airplane descended from about 10,000 feet down to about 7,800 feet while the ground speed of the airplane increased, as well as its rate of descent.
texts.1:
> "Shortly there after, credible witnesses that we've already spoken with described the airplane as being at an approximate level altitude with both wings folding backwards and the airplane going violently out of control," said McCarter.
McCarter adds the plane's radar data was lost at about 4,000 feet. Additionally, McCarter said the plane did not have a black box but officials did get two data cards out of the wreckage. Whether there is data on the cards remains to be seen.
Officials say the crash left a large debris field about half a mile long. If you live in the area and find debris on your property, you're asked to contact the Williamson County Sheriff’s Office at 615-790-5550.
Three dead after small plane crash in Williamson County (WZTV)
Witnesses to the accident or those who have surveillance video or other information that could be relevant to the investigation are asked to contact the NTSB at witness@ntsb.gov.
The wreckage is being reassembled in Springfield. Investigators say they will likely release a preliminary report before the end of the month.

May 29, 2024
RICHVALE AIRPLANE CRASH
Richvale, CA- On May 28, 2024, at approximately 1:48 p.m. the Butte County Sheriff’s Office (BCSO) dispatch center began receiving calls about an airplane crash at the Richvale Airport. Dispatchers determined a crop duster aircraft crashed at the end of the runway and the pilot was trapped inside the aircraft.
BCSO deputies, CAL-FIRE and medical personnel immediately responded. The pilot was removed from the aircraft and personnel immediately began providing lifesaving efforts. Despite the lifesaving efforts provided, the pilot did not survive. The pilot was identified as Hugh Mattingly, age 63, of Chico.
Deputies contacted the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) and the FAA. NTSB staff arrived at the Richvale Airport on May 29, 2024. The NTSB will oversee the investigation.

opened.information:
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century
Title: List of air show accidents and incidents in the 21st century
Chunks: 14,15,16,17,18,19,20,26,27,28,29,30
*   November 1 – Witham Field, Stuart, Florida – A pilot was killed while preparing for the Stuart Air Show when his Grumman OV-1 Mohawk crashed and caught fire when he failed to recover from an "overbank" roll.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-67)  
*   October 2 – Wings of Freedom Tour (Bradley International Airport, Hartford, Connecticut) – A Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress, owned by the Collings Foundation, crashed due to pilot error and engine/maintenance issues. Seven occupants of the 13 on board were killed and six were injured, along with one ground injury. The aircraft was destroyed by fire.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-68)  
*   June 21 – Troy, Ohio – Skip Stewart was forced to make an emergency landing on a county road in Troy in his Pitts S-2S after suffering an engine loss, just 6–7 miles (9.7–11.3 km) from the Dayton International Airport in Vandalia, Ohio, where he was set to take part in the Vectren Dayton Air Show.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-69)  
*   June 16 – Minnesota Air Spectacular (Mankato, Minnesota) – Kent Pietsch's Jelly Belly 1942 Interstate Cadet suffered damage from prop-wash that was caused by a nearby taxiing LockheedC-130 Hercules. The Interstate Cadet was in need of repairs; the C-130 Hercules was undamaged. No one involved in this accident suffered any sort of injury.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-70)  

*   June 15 – Płocki Piknik Lotniczy (Płock, Poland) – A pilot flying a Yakovlev Yak-52 was killed during an aerobatic display. The aircraft appeared to enter a flat spin. Late in the spin, the aircraft appeared to enter a more nose-down flight attitude, a common procedure used by pilots to exit a flat spin. Unfortunately, the aircraft was too low to recover and impacted the Wisła river, killing the single crewmember on board.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-71)  
*   February 19 – Isro Layout, Nagenahalli, India – Two BAE SystemsHawk Mk. 132 aircraft of the Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team collided midair during a rehearsal for Aero India 2019. They were about 17 km (11 mi) from the Yelahanka Air Force Station. Three people were involved in this accident: two pilots ejected safely while the third, Cdr. Sahil Gandhi, succumbed to his injuries.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-73)  
*   March 3 – Australian International Airshow (Avalon, Victoria, Australia) – A USAFC-17 had to abort its take-off run. Early in the take-off run, the number 4 engine ingested one of a flock of wedgetail eagles which had been milling around the airport. The plane suffered a major compressor stall, but safely aborted the take-off using emergency braking and thrust reversers on the undamaged engines.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-74)

*   October 12 – Culpeper Airfest (Culpeper Regional Airport, Culpeper, Virginia) – Jon Thocker, a member of the Redline Airshows Aerobatic Team, was killed when his [Van's RV-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van's_Aircraft_RV-8 "Van's Aircraft RV-8") crashed while performing a nighttime aerobatic routine.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-75) The NTSB concluded that his sense of attitude orientation was lost due to the lack of visual cues.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-76)  
*   August 11 – Abbotsford International Airshow (Abbotsford, Canada) – Four people were hospitalized, one critically, after a 1930s-era De Havilland Dragon Rapide biplane experienced a sudden loss of airspeed and crashed just after takeoff.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-77) The pilot's foot was amputated as a result of the accident.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-78) The Transportation Safety Board (TSB) concluded that the pilot encountered difficulties due to the complexity of a crosswind takeoff in a plane that already required a high workload during taxi and takeoff.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-79)  

*   July 7 – Borcea Air Base, Borcea, Romania – A MiG-21 Lancer crashed during an airshow. Rather than ejecting, witnesses said the pilot "stayed on board to fly the plane away from the crowd" of 3,000 attendees. The pilot, Florin Rotaru, was killed in the crash.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-80)  
*   June 2 – Gunfighter Skies Air and Space Celebration (Mountain Home Air Force Base, Idaho) – Dan Buchanan, a hang glider pilot, was killed when a developing vortex or dust devil caused him to lose control of his hang glider.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-82) Buchanan was a wheelchair-using aviator with more than 3,000 logged hours, who combined pilotage, music, and fire for his airshow performances.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-83)  
*   May 30 – Melville, Long Island, New York – Ken Johansen, a member of the GEICO Skytypers team, was killed when his SNJ-2 aircraft crashed due to aerodynamic stall.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-85) The pilot had flown at the Bethpage Air Show the week before and was en route to NAS Patuxent River for an upcoming airshow.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-86)  

*   April 25 – Shangjie Airport, Zhengzhou, China – Eglin Wells, an aerobatic pilot from Atlanta, Georgia, was killed when his custom-designed and -built Starjammer aircraft crashed while practicing for the Zhengzhou Air Show.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-88)  
*   April 4 – Nevada Test and Training Range, Nevada – Maj Stephen Del Bagno was killed when his F-16, Thunderbird No. 4, crashed during a routine aerial demonstration training flight.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-89) Del Bagno temporarily lost consciousness during a high G-force maneuver and became incapacitated prior to his fatal crash.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-90)  
*   March 31 – Warbirds Over Wanaka (Wanaka, New Zealand) – Warbird pilot Arthur Dovey was uninjured when his Yak-3 fighter collided with ground equipment that had been left on the grass runway, while landing after a display.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-91) The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) found that miscommunications meant that multiple pilots believed that the grass runway was available for landing while organizers believed that they would not be using it and so did not ensure that the ground equipment had been removed.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-93)  

*   February 6 – Singapore Airshow (Changi, Singapore) – A KAI T-50 Golden Eagle trainer from the Republic of Korea Air Force suffered a runway excursion and overturned during a formation takeoff. The pilot extricated himself from the plane and was uninjured in the accident.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-94)

*   September 24 –Terracina, Italy – Capt. Gabriele Orlandi of the Italian Air Force died while performing at an air show. The pilot did not have sufficient height to recover from a loop and his Eurofighter Typhoon crashed into the sea.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-95)  
*   September 2 – Chernyoe Airport, Balashikha, Russia – An AntonovAn-2 crashed at an air show after losing control while performing aerobatics, killing both pilots. The Interstate Aviation Committee (MAK) investigation found out that the Certificate of Airworthiness of the aircraft had expired in 2012. Additionally, both crew members did not have an An-2 type rating, and the aerobatics maneuvers performed by the aircraft were not allowed on the An-2.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-97)  
*   July 16 – Cummings, Kansas – Pilot, Vlado Lenoch, and passenger, Bethany Root, were killed when Lenoch's P-51D Mustang, "Baby Duck", crashed in a field.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-99) The plane had performed at the Amelia Earhart Festival the day before, was seen performing aerobatics before the accident and was flying at a low altitude for reasons that cannot be determined.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-100)  

*   June 5 – Brimpton Airfield (Reading, England) – A de Havilland Tiger Moth crashed at a fly-in to raise funds for the local air ambulance, injuring a spectator.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-127)  
*   June 2 – United States Air Force Academy graduation ceremony (Colorado Springs, Colorado, ) – Major Alex Turner, Thunderbird No. 6, crashed in a field after performing a flyover at the. The F-16 pilot ejected and was unhurt.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-128)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-129) A later investigation revealed that the aircraft's engine was inadvertently shutdown at the start of landing procedures, when a faulty throttle trigger permitted the throttle to be rotated into an engine cut-off position.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-130)  
*   June 2 – Smyrna, Tennessee – Capt. Jeff "Kooch" Kuss of the Blue Angels died just after takeoff while performing the Split-S maneuver in his F/A-18 Hornet during a practice run for The Great Tennessee Air Show. Capt. Kuss ejected, but his parachute was immediately engulfed in flames, causing him to fall to his death. Kuss' body was recovered multiple yards away from the crash site. The Navy investigation found that Capt. Kuss performed the maneuver at too low of an altitude while failing to retard the throttle out of afterburner, causing him to fall too fast and recover at too low of an altitude. The investigation also found weather conditions and pilot fatigue as contributing causes to the crash.The cause of death was blunt force trauma to the head.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-131)  

*   May 28 – Hudson River, New York – Pilot Bill Gordon died after crash landing P-47 Thunderbolt, "Jacky's Revenge", into the Hudson River while attempting an emergency landing after an engine failure.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-132)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-133) The plane was participating in a photo flight near the Statue of Liberty to promote the Jones Beach airshow taking place the following day.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-134)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-135)  
*   May 14 – Good Neighbor Day Air Show (DeKalb-Peachtree Airport, Chamblee, Georgia) – Aerobatic pilot Greg Connell crashed and died during a performance, while piloting his self-modified Pitts-12, "Connell Model 12".[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-136)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-137)[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-138)  

*   April 17 – Cozumel Aero Show (Cozumel, Quintana Roo, Mexico) – Guatemalan pilot Juan Miguel García Salas died when his Extra EA-300L aerobatics plane crashed in a wooded area near Aeródromo Capitán Eduardo Toledo.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-139) The Directorate General of Civil Aeronautics, now the Federal Civil Aviation Agency (AFAC), found that this was likely the result of a G-LOC.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-140)

*   December 20 – Air Force Flight School 70th Anniversary (Yogyakarta, Indonesia) – Two pilots, Lt. Col. Marda Sarjono and Capt. Diwi Cahyadi, were killed when their KAI T-50I Golden Eagle crashed during a performance.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-141)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-142)  
*   October 18 – Wings Over Houston (Harris County, Texas) – A skydiver was injured when he landed on a supply tent. It was reported that he did not hear the order cancelling the formation jump due to high winds.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-143)  
*   September 12 – Wings Over Big South Fork Air & Car Show (Scott County, Tennessee) – An Aero L-39 Albatros jet, piloted by Jay "Flash" Gordon of Louisville, Kentucky, crashed approximately two minutes after take-off due to an engine loss. The pilot was pronounced dead on scene.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-144)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-145)  

*   August 29 – Stewart International Airport, Newburgh , New York – An aerobatic pilot was killed when his 1998 Giles G-202 single-engine plane crashed in a marshy area while he was practicing for the New York Air Show.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-146) The investigation found that the vertical and horizontal stabilizers had separated from the plane, likely due to bad construction.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-147)  
*   August 23 – Dittingen, Basel, Switzerland – Two of three C-42B light aircraft flying in formation crashed after they touched in mid-air at an airshow. One pilot was killed when the automatic rescue system on his plane failed to activate and the aircraft crashed into a barn.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-148) The Swiss Transportation Safety Investigation Board (SUST) concluded that the pilots failed to see and avoid each other due to incomplete formation flying training.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-149)

*   November 1 – Witham Field, Stuart, Florida – A pilot was killed while preparing for the Stuart Air Show when his Grumman OV-1 Mohawk crashed and caught fire when he failed to recover from an "overbank" roll.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-67)  
*   October 2 – Wings of Freedom Tour (Bradley International Airport, Hartford, Connecticut) – A Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress, owned by the Collings Foundation, crashed due to pilot error and engine/maintenance issues. Seven occupants of the 13 on board were killed and six were injured, along with one ground injury. The aircraft was destroyed by fire.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-68)  
*   June 21 – Troy, Ohio – Skip Stewart was forced to make an emergency landing on a county road in Troy in his Pitts S-2S after suffering an engine loss, just 6–7 miles (9.7–11.3 km) from the Dayton International Airport in Vandalia, Ohio, where he was set to take part in the Vectren Dayton Air Show.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-69)  
*   June 16 – Minnesota Air Spectacular (Mankato, Minnesota) – Kent Pietsch's Jelly Belly 1942 Interstate Cadet suffered damage from prop-wash that was caused by a nearby taxiing LockheedC-130 Hercules. The Interstate Cadet was in need of repairs; the C-130 Hercules was undamaged. No one involved in this accident suffered any sort of injury.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-70)
texts.15:
*   June 15 – Płocki Piknik Lotniczy (Płock, Poland) – A pilot flying a Yakovlev Yak-52 was killed during an aerobatic display. The aircraft appeared to enter a flat spin. Late in the spin, the aircraft appeared to enter a more nose-down flight attitude, a common procedure used by pilots to exit a flat spin. Unfortunately, the aircraft was too low to recover and impacted the Wisła river, killing the single crewmember on board.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-71)  
*   February 19 – Isro Layout, Nagenahalli, India – Two BAE SystemsHawk Mk. 132 aircraft of the Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team collided midair during a rehearsal for Aero India 2019. They were about 17 km (11 mi) from the Yelahanka Air Force Station. Three people were involved in this accident: two pilots ejected safely while the third, Cdr. Sahil Gandhi, succumbed to his injuries.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-73)  
*   March 3 – Australian International Airshow (Avalon, Victoria, Australia) – A USAFC-17 had to abort its take-off run. Early in the take-off run, the number 4 engine ingested one of a flock of wedgetail eagles which had been milling around the airport. The plane suffered a major compressor stall, but safely aborted the take-off using emergency braking and thrust reversers on the undamaged engines.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-74)

*   May 30 – Melville, Long Island, New York – Ken Johansen, a member of the GEICO Skytypers team, was killed when his SNJ-2 aircraft crashed due to aerodynamic stall.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-85) The pilot had flown at the Bethpage Air Show the week before and was en route to NAS Patuxent River for an upcoming airshow.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-86)
texts.18:
*   April 25 – Shangjie Airport, Zhengzhou, China – Eglin Wells, an aerobatic pilot from Atlanta, Georgia, was killed when his custom-designed and -built Starjammer aircraft crashed while practicing for the Zhengzhou Air Show.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-88)  
*   April 4 – Nevada Test and Training Range, Nevada – Maj Stephen Del Bagno was killed when his F-16, Thunderbird No. 4, crashed during a routine aerial demonstration training flight.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-89) Del Bagno temporarily lost consciousness during a high G-force maneuver and became incapacitated prior to his fatal crash.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-90)  
*   March 31 – Warbirds Over Wanaka (Wanaka, New Zealand) – Warbird pilot Arthur Dovey was uninjured when his Yak-3 fighter collided with ground equipment that had been left on the grass runway, while landing after a display.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-91) The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) found that miscommunications meant that multiple pilots believed that the grass runway was available for landing while organizers believed that they would not be using it and so did not ensure that the ground equipment had been removed.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-93)
texts.19: *   February 6 – Singapore Airshow (Changi, Singapore) – A KAI T-50 Golden Eagle trainer from the Republic of Korea Air Force suffered a runway excursion and overturned during a formation takeoff. The pilot extricated himself from the plane and was uninjured in the accident.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-94)
texts.20:
*   September 24 –Terracina, Italy – Capt. Gabriele Orlandi of the Italian Air Force died while performing at an air show. The pilot did not have sufficient height to recover from a loop and his Eurofighter Typhoon crashed into the sea.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-95)  
*   September 2 – Chernyoe Airport, Balashikha, Russia – An AntonovAn-2 crashed at an air show after losing control while performing aerobatics, killing both pilots. The Interstate Aviation Committee (MAK) investigation found out that the Certificate of Airworthiness of the aircraft had expired in 2012. Additionally, both crew members did not have an An-2 type rating, and the aerobatics maneuvers performed by the aircraft were not allowed on the An-2.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-97)  
*   July 16 – Cummings, Kansas – Pilot, Vlado Lenoch, and passenger, Bethany Root, were killed when Lenoch's P-51D Mustang, "Baby Duck", crashed in a field.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-99) The plane had performed at the Amelia Earhart Festival the day before, was seen performing aerobatics before the accident and was flying at a low altitude for reasons that cannot be determined.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-100)
texts.26:
*   June 5 – Brimpton Airfield (Reading, England) – A de Havilland Tiger Moth crashed at a fly-in to raise funds for the local air ambulance, injuring a spectator.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-127)  
*   June 2 – United States Air Force Academy graduation ceremony (Colorado Springs, Colorado, ) – Major Alex Turner, Thunderbird No. 6, crashed in a field after performing a flyover at the. The F-16 pilot ejected and was unhurt.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-128)[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-129) A later investigation revealed that the aircraft's engine was inadvertently shutdown at the start of landing procedures, when a faulty throttle trigger permitted the throttle to be rotated into an engine cut-off position.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-130)  
*   June 2 – Smyrna, Tennessee – Capt. Jeff "Kooch" Kuss of the Blue Angels died just after takeoff while performing the Split-S maneuver in his F/A-18 Hornet during a practice run for The Great Tennessee Air Show. Capt. Kuss ejected, but his parachute was immediately engulfed in flames, causing him to fall to his death. Kuss' body was recovered multiple yards away from the crash site. The Navy investigation found that Capt. Kuss performed the maneuver at too low of an altitude while failing to retard the throttle out of afterburner, causing him to fall too fast and recover at too low of an altitude. The investigation also found weather conditions and pilot fatigue as contributing causes to the crash.The cause of death was blunt force trauma to the head.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-131)
texts.27:
*   May 28 – Hudson River, New York – Pilot Bill Gordon died after crash landing P-47 Thunderbolt, "Jacky's Revenge", into the Hudson River while attempting an emergency landing after an engine failure.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-132)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-133) The plane was participating in a photo flight near the Statue of Liberty to promote the Jones Beach airshow taking place the following day.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-134)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-135)  
*   May 14 – Good Neighbor Day Air Show (DeKalb-Peachtree Airport, Chamblee, Georgia) – Aerobatic pilot Greg Connell crashed and died during a performance, while piloting his self-modified Pitts-12, "Connell Model 12".[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-136)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-137)[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-138)
texts.28: *   April 17 – Cozumel Aero Show (Cozumel, Quintana Roo, Mexico) – Guatemalan pilot Juan Miguel García Salas died when his Extra EA-300L aerobatics plane crashed in a wooded area near Aeródromo Capitán Eduardo Toledo.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-139) The Directorate General of Civil Aeronautics, now the Federal Civil Aviation Agency (AFAC), found that this was likely the result of a G-LOC.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-140)
texts.29:
*   December 20 – Air Force Flight School 70th Anniversary (Yogyakarta, Indonesia) – Two pilots, Lt. Col. Marda Sarjono and Capt. Diwi Cahyadi, were killed when their KAI T-50I Golden Eagle crashed during a performance.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-141)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-142)  
*   October 18 – Wings Over Houston (Harris County, Texas) – A skydiver was injured when he landed on a supply tent. It was reported that he did not hear the order cancelling the formation jump due to high winds.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-143)  
*   September 12 – Wings Over Big South Fork Air & Car Show (Scott County, Tennessee) – An Aero L-39 Albatros jet, piloted by Jay "Flash" Gordon of Louisville, Kentucky, crashed approximately two minutes after take-off due to an engine loss. The pilot was pronounced dead on scene.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-144)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-145)
texts.30:
*   August 29 – Stewart International Airport, Newburgh , New York – An aerobatic pilot was killed when his 1998 Giles G-202 single-engine plane crashed in a marshy area while he was practicing for the New York Air Show.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-146) The investigation found that the vertical and horizontal stabilizers had separated from the plane, likely due to bad construction.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-147)  
*   August 23 – Dittingen, Basel, Switzerland – Two of three C-42B light aircraft flying in formation crashed after they touched in mid-air at an airshow. One pilot was killed when the automatic rescue system on his plane failed to activate and the aircraft crashed into a barn.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-148) The Swiss Transportation Safety Investigation Board (SUST) concluded that the pilots failed to see and avoid each other due to incomplete formation flying training.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_air_show_accidents_and_incidents_in_the_21st_century#cite_note-149)

EDITOR’S NOTE: For the latest developments, follow our updated coverage here.
A private jet traveling from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas careened into the ground in Palm Beach County, Florida, Sunday afternoon, leaving a deep crater and burning debris just feet from nearby homes and businesses and killing all nine on board, officials say.
Video from a passing vehicle shows the jet, a Learjet 60, slamming down nose first on a busy roadway in a flash before a fireball erupts.
“It was a cataclysmic plane crash,” Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said. “It looked like a missile going down.”

The jet descended 27,000 feet over the course of one minute, just before flight tracking data cut off, the website ADS-B Exchange shows.
Officials have not said what caused the jet to crash, and they have not identified the nine who died or said how many were passengers and crew.

There were scattered storms in the area at the time, and the plane passed through a stronger storm cell a few minutes before it began descending, but it is unclear if the storm contributed to the crash.

## ‘I heard and felt the boom’
The crash marks the second deadliest plane crash in the United States this year, according to NTSB records, after 12 people died in June when a skydiving plane crashed in Butler, Missouri. It is also the worst crash involving a Learjet 60, according to data from the Flight Safety Foundation. In 2008, four people were killed when a Learjet 60 bound for Los Angeles crashed on takeoff from Columbia, South Carolina.
The plane hit the ground shortly before 1 p.m. on Military Trail, a major thoroughfare between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North, the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office said.The roadway was left shattered and burning debris dotted the crater, video from CNN affiliate WPBF showed.
“There is a lot of debris that was strewn as a result of this crash,” DeSantis said.
The scene is just miles from the airport in West Palm Beach that was recently renamed for President Donald Trump and his Mar-A-Lago resort.
About 600 people are in need of shelter because the damage on the ground is blocking the entrance of a mobile home park, said Joel Flores, Palm Beach County commissioner for District 3, who was the first county official at the scene. Residents are being sent to two shelters in the county while the site is being investigated, he said.
“I heard and felt the boom,” Andrew Mannino told CNN. “The power immediately went out and is still out.”
Mannino said he smelled the smoke and “saw a large black cloud immerse in the air.”
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called the crash a “horrific tragedy.”
Dash cam video showing the crash is going to be important to investigators piecing together what happened, said Mary Schiavo, CNN aviation analyst and former inspector general for the Transportation Department.
“That is not a controlled descent,” Schiavo told CNN’s Fredricka Whitfield Sunday. “It’s clear, whatever happened, they had lost control of the plane.”
The steep descent could have forced parts of the plane to break off and the flight data recorder could have been destroyed in the explosion, she added.
Investigators will also have to piece together whether the environment played a part in the crash.

## ‘I heard and felt the boom’
Ice on wings and other surfaces can also pose a major threat to private jets. In January 2024, the NTSB published a safety alert underscoring the risks of in-flight icing conditions, which can cause pilots to lose control. The agency warned ice can “make managing the airplane’s flightpath and airspeed more difficult and can prevent the airplane from maintaining level flight.”

Title: Jet nosedives and erupts into fireball near busy roadway in South Florida, killing all 9 passengers
Chunks: 0,1,2
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. -- A business jet carrying nine people nose-dived into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday and erupted into a giant fireball that appeared to just miss homes near a busy roadway. Everyone on board was killed, the nation's transportation secretary said.
Video recorded by people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the Bahamas-bound aircraft plunged from the sky before striking near the Palm Beach County roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining a crater as people milled about, expressing shock that it landed only feet from homes and inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy posted on X that the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County at 12:50 p.m. and called it a "horrific tragedy." The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board's investigation, he said.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground injured or killed.
"It was a cataclysmic plane crash," DeSantis told reporters at the scene. "It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road."
Rain pounded the region on Sunday. A flood watch due to excessive rainfall was in effect through Monday afternoon, the National Weather Service said.
The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.
The plane was heading east at 35,000 feet (about 11 kilometers) when pilots reported turbulence, icing and precipitation and requested to climb another 2,000 feet (about 610 meters).
Moments later, the plane entered a steep dive, first 10,000 feet per minute, then 20,000 feet per minute and up to 30,000 feet per minute, speeding the plane beyond its design limits, according to air traffic control recordings and flight tracking data.
A pilot declared an emergency and issued distress calls. The plane banked sharply to the right before it smashed into the ground.

Minutes before the crash, the pilot reported ice accumulating on the jet and turbulence that was jolting it by as much as 700 feet (213 meters), according to air traffic control recordings captured by LiveATC.net.
"We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence," the pilot told controllers.

## Top Stories
But the situation rapidly deteriorated. After encountering precipitation and requesting to climb, the pilot declared an emergency as the aircraft began losing altitude at an alarming rate.
"We're descending 8,000 - mayday, mayday - we're descending 10,000 feet per minute," the pilot radioed.
"We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute," the pilot radioed, before delivering a devastating acknowledgment of what was about to happen. "We're going to crash into the ground."
Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, said the jet was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.
Steve Arroyo, an aviation safety expert, said icing and turbulence could have been factors in the crash and may have caused the plane to stall while it was cruising at 34,000 feet (10,363 meters).
There are many potential factors and the NTSB will consider all of them, including how the pilot responded to the icing and turbulence reported over the radio. But investigators won't rule anything out at this early stage, he said.
The NTSB said investigators were expected to arrive at the crash site on Sunday and Monday. A media briefing is scheduled for Monday in West Palm Beach.
Palm Beach County authorities were evacuating about 600 people from a nearby mobile home community while federal officials investigate the crash. The road will be closed until further notice, county officials said.
The crash occurred in Greenacres, Florida, according to Palm Beach County sheriff's officials. The city of 45,000 people is about 7 miles (11 kilometers) southwest of West Palm Beach.
___
_Taxin reported from Santa Ana, California. AP Transportation Writer Josh Funk contributed from Gretna, Nebraska._

# ‘Experimental, homebuilt’ plane goes down in Wakulla County over the weekend, leaves one dead
The National Transportation Safety Board is currently investigating a plane crash that happened over the weekend in Wakulla County, leaving one person dead.
By WCTV Staff, Chasity Maynard and Jamiya Coleman
Published: May 27, 2024 at 11:17 PM UTC|Updated: May 29, 2024 at 9:38 PM UTC
Share
Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google
TALLAHASSEE, Fla. (WCTV) - The National Transportation Safety Board is currently investigating a plane crash that happened over the weekend in Wakulla County, leaving one person dead.
The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission said 82-year-old Frank Clementi of Wesley Chapel, Florida died in the weekend plane crash. He was the only occupant on the plane, according to the FWC.
The NTSB said the crash happened Saturday around 10 p.m. near Panacea.
“NTSB is investigating the crash of an experimental, homebuilt Glasair 1 airplane near Panacea, Florida on May 25,” a statement from the NTSB said.
It involved an experimental home-built plane that investigators say went down in the Apalachee bay. The airplane was traveling from Destin to Zephyr Hills, according to the safety board.

# ‘Experimental, homebuilt’ plane goes down in Wakulla County over the weekend, leaves one dead
The National Transportation Safety Board is currently investigating a plane crash that happened over the weekend in Wakulla County, leaving one person dead.
By WCTV Staff, Chasity Maynard and Jamiya Coleman
Published: May 27, 2024 at 11:17 PM UTC|Updated: May 29, 2024 at 9:38 PM UTC
Share
Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google
TALLAHASSEE, Fla. (WCTV) - The National Transportation Safety Board is currently investigating a plane crash that happened over the weekend in Wakulla County, leaving one person dead.
The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission said 82-year-old Frank Clementi of Wesley Chapel, Florida died in the weekend plane crash. He was the only occupant on the plane, according to the FWC.
The NTSB said the crash happened Saturday around 10 p.m. near Panacea.
“NTSB is investigating the crash of an experimental, homebuilt Glasair 1 airplane near Panacea, Florida on May 25,” a statement from the NTSB said.
It involved an experimental home-built plane that investigators say went down in the Apalachee bay. The airplane was traveling from Destin to Zephyr Hills, according to the safety board.

EDITOR’S NOTE: For the latest developments, follow our updated coverage here.
A private jet traveling from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas careened into the ground in Palm Beach County, Florida, Sunday afternoon, leaving a deep crater and burning debris just feet from nearby homes and businesses and killing all nine on board, officials say.
Video from a passing vehicle shows the jet, a Learjet 60, slamming down nose first on a busy roadway in a flash before a fireball erupts.
“It was a cataclysmic plane crash,” Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said. “It looked like a missile going down.”

There were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground injured.

Before the crash,the pilot calmly reported ice accumulating on the aircraft, with an outside air temperature of -47 degrees Celsius, and moderate turbulence, bouncing the plane by up to 700 feet, according to a recording of air traffic control radio calls captured by LiveATC.net.
But moments later, the pilot began to sound more panicked.
“Mayday, mayday,” the pilot told the Miami Air Route Traffic Control Center. “We’re descending 10,000 feet per minute!”
“We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute,” they yelled, “We’re going to crash into the ground!”
Audio captures moments before Learjet crash
Minutes before the crash, the pilot of the plane reported ice accumulating on the aircraft, an outside air temperature of -47 degrees Celsius, and moderate turbulence.
Source: LiveATC.com
The jet descended 27,000 feet over the course of one minute, just before flight tracking data cut off, the website ADS-B Exchange shows.
Officials have not said what caused the jet to crash, and they have not identified the nine who died or said how many were passengers and crew.

## ‘I heard and felt the boom’
The crash marks the second deadliest plane crash in the United States this year, according to NTSB records, after 12 people died in June when a skydiving plane crashed in Butler, Missouri. It is also the worst crash involving a Learjet 60, according to data from the Flight Safety Foundation. In 2008, four people were killed when a Learjet 60 bound for Los Angeles crashed on takeoff from Columbia, South Carolina.
The plane hit the ground shortly before 1 p.m. on Military Trail, a major thoroughfare between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North, the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office said.The roadway was left shattered and burning debris dotted the crater, video from CNN affiliate WPBF showed.
“There is a lot of debris that was strewn as a result of this crash,” DeSantis said.
The scene is just miles from the airport in West Palm Beach that was recently renamed for President Donald Trump and his Mar-A-Lago resort.
About 600 people are in need of shelter because the damage on the ground is blocking the entrance of a mobile home park, said Joel Flores, Palm Beach County commissioner for District 3, who was the first county official at the scene. Residents are being sent to two shelters in the county while the site is being investigated, he said.
“I heard and felt the boom,” Andrew Mannino told CNN. “The power immediately went out and is still out.”
Mannino said he smelled the smoke and “saw a large black cloud immerse in the air.”
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called the crash a “horrific tragedy.”
Dash cam video showing the crash is going to be important to investigators piecing together what happened, said Mary Schiavo, CNN aviation analyst and former inspector general for the Transportation Department.
“That is not a controlled descent,” Schiavo told CNN’s Fredricka Whitfield Sunday. “It’s clear, whatever happened, they had lost control of the plane.”
The steep descent could have forced parts of the plane to break off and the flight data recorder could have been destroyed in the explosion, she added.
Investigators will also have to piece together whether the environment played a part in the crash.

## ‘I heard and felt the boom’
Ice on wings and other surfaces can also pose a major threat to private jets. In January 2024, the NTSB published a safety alert underscoring the risks of in-flight icing conditions, which can cause pilots to lose control. The agency warned ice can “make managing the airplane’s flightpath and airspeed more difficult and can prevent the airplane from maintaining level flight.”

WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. -- A business jet carrying nine people nose-dived into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday and erupted into a giant fireball that appeared to just miss homes near a busy roadway. Everyone on board was killed, the nation's transportation secretary said.
Video recorded by people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the Bahamas-bound aircraft plunged from the sky before striking near the Palm Beach County roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining a crater as people milled about, expressing shock that it landed only feet from homes and inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy posted on X that the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach County at 12:50 p.m. and called it a "horrific tragedy." The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board's investigation, he said.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground injured or killed.
"It was a cataclysmic plane crash," DeSantis told reporters at the scene. "It looked like a missile going down and left a big crater on the side of the road."
Rain pounded the region on Sunday. A flood watch due to excessive rainfall was in effect through Monday afternoon, the National Weather Service said.
The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.
The plane was heading east at 35,000 feet (about 11 kilometers) when pilots reported turbulence, icing and precipitation and requested to climb another 2,000 feet (about 610 meters).
Moments later, the plane entered a steep dive, first 10,000 feet per minute, then 20,000 feet per minute and up to 30,000 feet per minute, speeding the plane beyond its design limits, according to air traffic control recordings and flight tracking data.
A pilot declared an emergency and issued distress calls. The plane banked sharply to the right before it smashed into the ground.
texts.1:
Minutes before the crash, the pilot reported ice accumulating on the jet and turbulence that was jolting it by as much as 700 feet (213 meters), according to air traffic control recordings captured by LiveATC.net.
"We have light, clear ice that is manageable and moderate turbulence," the pilot told controllers.
texts.2:
## Top Stories
But the situation rapidly deteriorated. After encountering precipitation and requesting to climb, the pilot declared an emergency as the aircraft began losing altitude at an alarming rate.
"We're descending 8,000 - mayday, mayday - we're descending 10,000 feet per minute," the pilot radioed.
"We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute," the pilot radioed, before delivering a devastating acknowledgment of what was about to happen. "We're going to crash into the ground."
Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, said the jet was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.
Steve Arroyo, an aviation safety expert, said icing and turbulence could have been factors in the crash and may have caused the plane to stall while it was cruising at 34,000 feet (10,363 meters).
There are many potential factors and the NTSB will consider all of them, including how the pilot responded to the icing and turbulence reported over the radio. But investigators won't rule anything out at this early stage, he said.
The NTSB said investigators were expected to arrive at the crash site on Sunday and Monday. A media briefing is scheduled for Monday in West Palm Beach.
Palm Beach County authorities were evacuating about 600 people from a nearby mobile home community while federal officials investigate the crash. The road will be closed until further notice, county officials said.
The crash occurred in Greenacres, Florida, according to Palm Beach County sheriff's officials. The city of 45,000 people is about 7 miles (11 kilometers) southwest of West Palm Beach.
___
_Taxin reported from Santa Ana, California. AP Transportation Writer Josh Funk contributed from Gretna, Nebraska._

EDITOR’S NOTE: For the latest developments, follow our updated coverage here.
A private jet traveling from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas careened into the ground in Palm Beach County, Florida, Sunday afternoon, leaving a deep crater and burning debris just feet from nearby homes and businesses and killing all nine on board, officials say.
Video from a passing vehicle shows the jet, a Learjet 60, slamming down nose first on a busy roadway in a flash before a fireball erupts.
“It was a cataclysmic plane crash,” Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said. “It looked like a missile going down.”
Ad Feedback
There were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground injured.

0:15
Before the crash,the pilot calmly reported ice accumulating on the aircraft, with an outside air temperature of -47 degrees Celsius, and moderate turbulence, bouncing the plane by up to 700 feet, according to a recording of air traffic control radio calls captured by LiveATC.net.
But moments later, the pilot began to sound more panicked.
“Mayday, mayday,” the pilot told the Miami Air Route Traffic Control Center. “We’re descending 10,000 feet per minute!”
“We are in an overspeed condition descending 20,000 feet per minute,” they yelled, “We’re going to crash into the ground!”
Audio captures moments before Learjet crash
Minutes before the crash, the pilot of the plane reported ice accumulating on the aircraft, an outside air temperature of -47 degrees Celsius, and moderate turbulence.
Source: LiveATC.com
The jet descended 27,000 feet over the course of one minute, just before flight tracking data cut off, the website ADS-B Exchange shows.
Officials have not said what caused the jet to crash, and they have not identified the nine who died or said how many were passengers and crew.

There were scattered storms in the area at the time, and the plane passed through a stronger storm cell a few minutes before it began descending, but it is unclear if the storm contributed to the crash.
A news conference is expected Monday as authorities from the Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board investigate.’

0:20

## ‘I heard and felt the boom’
The crash marks the second deadliest plane crash in the United States this year, according to NTSB records, after 12 people died in June when a skydiving plane crashed in Butler, Missouri. It is also the worst crash involving a Learjet 60, according to data from the Flight Safety Foundation. In 2008, four people were killed when a Learjet 60 bound for Los Angeles crashed on takeoff from Columbia, South Carolina.
The plane hit the ground shortly before 1 p.m. on Military Trail, a major thoroughfare between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North, the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office said.The roadway was left shattered and burning debris dotted the crater, video from CNN affiliate WPBF showed.
“There is a lot of debris that was strewn as a result of this crash,” DeSantis said.
The scene is just miles from the airport in West Palm Beach that was recently renamed for President Donald Trump and his Mar-A-Lago resort.
About 600 people are in need of shelter because the damage on the ground is blocking the entrance of a mobile home park, said Joel Flores, Palm Beach County commissioner for District 3, who was the first county official at the scene. Residents are being sent to two shelters in the county while the site is being investigated, he said.
“I heard and felt the boom,” Andrew Mannino told CNN. “The power immediately went out and is still out.”
Mannino said he smelled the smoke and “saw a large black cloud immerse in the air.”
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called the crash a “horrific tragedy.”
Dash cam video showing the crash is going to be important to investigators piecing together what happened, said Mary Schiavo, CNN aviation analyst and former inspector general for the Transportation Department.
“That is not a controlled descent,” Schiavo told CNN’s Fredricka Whitfield Sunday. “It’s clear, whatever happened, they had lost control of the plane.”
The steep descent could have forced parts of the plane to break off and the flight data recorder could have been destroyed in the explosion, she added.
Investigators will also have to piece together whether the environment played a part in the crash.

## ‘I heard and felt the boom’
Ice on wings and other surfaces can also pose a major threat to private jets. In January 2024, the NTSB published a safety alert underscoring the risks of in-flight icing conditions, which can cause pilots to lose control. The agency warned ice can “make managing the airplane’s flightpath and airspeed more difficult and can prevent the airplane from maintaining level flight.”

It’s not clear if the plane had a cockpit voice recorder on board, but FAA regulations require jet aircraft with more than one engine to carry a voice recorder if they are flown for hire.
The plane is registered to an LLC in Delaware, according to FAA records, and is listed as available for charter online.
_This story has been updated with additional information._
CNN meteorologist Tyler Ory and CNN’s Amanda Jackson and Nic Anderson contributed to this report.

About 600 people are in need of shelter because the damage on the ground is blocking the entrance of a mobile home park, said Joel Flores, Palm Beach County commissioner for District 3, who was the first county official at the scene. Residents are being sent to two shelters in the county while the site is being investigated, he said.
“I heard and felt the boom,” Andrew Mannino told CNN. “The power immediately went out and is still out.”
Mannino said he smelled the smoke and “saw a large black cloud immerse in the air.”
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called the crash a “horrific tragedy.”
Dash cam video showing the crash is going to be important to investigators piecing together what happened, said Mary Schiavo, CNN aviation analyst and former inspector general for the Transportation Department.
“That is not a controlled descent,” Schiavo told CNN’s Fredricka Whitfield Sunday. “It’s clear, whatever happened, they had lost control of the plane.”
The steep descent could have forced parts of the plane to break off and the flight data recorder could have been destroyed in the explosion, she added.
Investigators will also have to piece together whether the environment played a part in the crash.

Ice on wings and other surfaces can also pose a major threat to private jets. In January 2024, the NTSB published a safety alert underscoring the risks of in-flight icing conditions, which can cause pilots to lose control. The agency warned ice can “make managing the airplane’s flightpath and airspeed more difficult and can prevent the airplane from maintaining level flight.”

Area resident Anthony Blackmon told NBC South Floridathat he was about 500 feet away when the plane went down.
“Debris was everywhere. Debris hit my house. Everything was on fire. The road was on fire,” Blackmon said.
The aircraft is registered to a limited liability company in Delaware, according to FAA records.
Learjet manufacturer Bombardier said in a statement that the company is “deeply saddened by this tragic event and extend our sincerest sympathies to all those affected.”
“We cannot comment on the potential cause of this accident until the investigation is complete and we will fully support the investigating authorities and cooperate as needed,” Bombardier said.
The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating the crash.
The Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office said an aircraft incident was under investigation in the area of Military Trail, and all northbound and southbound lanes were closed until further notice.
